title: Universal Life Insurance Service Desk Rules: Beneficiary Designations
content:
**Rule.** The owner of an Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy names primary and contingent beneficiaries.

- A beneficiary designation is recorded only while the policy status is applied, in force, in the grace period or overloan protected, as the policy record shows.
- A changed designation is recorded only from a beneficiary change request signed by the owner and, where the current designation names an irrevocable beneficiary, also signed in consent by that beneficiary. Whether a current beneficiary is irrevocable is read from the designation on record.
- The new designation replaces the earlier one entirely and is effective on the owner's signature date if signed while the insured was living; Ashgrove is discharged for payments made before receipt.
- Shares are whole percents of at least the tier's smallest share, totalling 100 in each class, with no more than the tier's maximum number of primaries.
- No change is accepted after the insured's death.

## Points of judgement

| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Change requested on a lapsed or surrendered policy | Not recorded; the status is not one of applied, in force, grace period or overloan protected |
| Current designation names an irrevocable beneficiary who has not signed in consent | The change is not recorded |
| Primary shares of 60% and 40% | Valid: whole percents totalling 100 |
| Primary shares of 50.5% and 49.5% | Not valid: shares must be whole percents |
| Contingent shares totalling 90% | Not valid: each class totals 100 |
| Change request received after the insured's death | Not accepted |

## Hypothetical illustration

An owner signs a change naming a new primary on 3 April; the insured is living on that date and the request reaches Ashgrove on 10 April. The new designation is effective from 3 April and replaces the old one entirely; a payment Ashgrove made on 5 April under the old designation, before receipt, discharges Ashgrove for that payment.
